slides.title: Key questions

paragraphs.text: Key questions
Should Brightwork launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027, and if so, how should it be packaged and priced to lift NRR from 101% to 105% by 2028 with gross margin at or above 75%?
Will customers value Copilot enough to pay for it as an add-on?
Which package and price earns the most within the 75% margin floor?
How much is Routewise's AI costing us in deals and churn?
Is a Q2 2027 launch worth delaying the mobile app rewrite?
How should we launch, and what would change the plan?
Decision maker
Success criteria
Timing
Out of scope
CEO and executive team: launch timing, package and price
Net revenue retention rises from 101% to 105% by 2028; Company gross margin stays at or above 75%; The trade-off with the mobile app rewrite is made explicitly
January 2027 planning
Changes to the Core plan price; Building or switching AI models; Engineering beyond the 60 engineers in the plan

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Launch Copilot in Q4 2027, after the mobile rewrite, in a $12-a-seat Pro plan, not a $149 add-on
Customers value Copilot, but only about one in seven will pay for it as an add-on
–	Beta volunteers gained 9 percentage points more output per dispatcher-hour than matched accounts
–	Only 14% of beta accounts paid $149 a month, against 46% stated intent
A Pro plan at $12 more per seat with a request allowance beats the add-on within the margin floor
–	The add-on yields about $0.85M of gross profit a year, not $8M of ARR
–	Pro adds $2.9M of ARR and reaches 2.4 times as many accounts
Routewise's AI is a smaller threat than claimed; mobile reliability loses far more customers
–	Even the whole win-rate fall is worth at most $0.64M of ARR a year
–	Mobile reliability drives 27% of churn, against 6% for AI features
Shipping the mobile rewrite first protects about twice the ARR that waiting on Copilot risks
–	A mobile slip risks up to $1.09M of ARR, against $0.56M for Copilot
–	A Q4 2027 Pro launch still closes the NRR gap if 26% of accounts move
Approve Pro now, test its price, and launch in Q4 2027 unless the win rate says AI cannot wait
–	A win rate still near 37% after the discount would bring the launch forward
